justification: Carrying span: 'The river below it is thick with dace; one afternoon's netting last May took four hundred-odd of them, more than the trap has held in fifteen years', set against the book's own tally of 31 dace. A killed on 'Since the pass opened in 2011 the trap has been emptied most mornings of the run, the counts written into a hardbacked book' - the book begins in 2011; 1931 is only when the mill stopped, and the weir merely 'held water for' that mill. C killed for want of any span: 'The first nine springs are in one hand, the rest in three others' is about handwriting, not misidentification. D inverted by that same span - one hand did the first nine, three others the rest.

Carrying span: 'Of 74 tagged, 61 reached the weir, 54 on the left, and 39 went into the pass... Twelve came out at the top' - 27 of 39 failed, i.e. most. A killed on 'Of the eleven that entered above ten degrees, seven got out; of the twenty-eight that entered colder, five did' (roughly 64 per cent against 18). B killed on 'The pools do not help. They are short, and at April flows the jet from one notch reaches the wall of the next; there is no quiet corner in them.' C killed on 'A grayling is deep through the body and carries a dorsal fin like a sail' - the stated obstacle is build, and raw strength has already been set aside earlier in the piece.

Carrying span: 'They don't find it, and they don't find it because they don't come up that side of the river', with the too-little-flow half supplied by 'The pass releases about a quarter of a cubic metre a second; in April the river brings down nine. Four metres out from the mouth there is nothing of that quarter left to follow.' B killed on 'thinks strength has little to do with it', which is the passage explicitly discarding the fall-height account. C killed for want of any span - the trap is emptied 'most mornings of the run' and no seasonal opening date is given. D killed on 'Nine went in. Five came out at the top' - dace do enter individually, so no refusal to leave the shoal is on offer.

Carrying span: 'The other, three walls further up, came through the same water clear' - the passage holds the water constant and varies only position, so the implication carried is positional. A killed by that same 'the same water' clause: an identical spate did not pack the upper orifice, so the spate's force cannot be what singles out the lower one. B killed on the stated purpose, 'so a fish could go through a wall instead of over it'. D killed on 'two of the nine cross-walls were cut' plus 'it is still packed' - seven walls are uncut and one of the two cut ones is blocked.

The spine is three species with three outcomes and two distinct causes: trout, of which 'a trout goes up without appearing to try'; dace, who 'don't find it... because they don't come up that side of the river'; grayling, who enter 'as a fish that lives in the current would' but of whom 'Whatever stops them is inside.' A killed because the river above the weir is never discussed. B inverted by 'Nobody says the pass does not work. What has taken fifteen years to become interesting is what it works for' - the counts are the thing interrogated, not evidence marshalled for a thesis about throughput. C killed on proportion: the 2023 orifices occupy the closing three sentences, not the argument.

Carrying span: 'Where the glue went in, the sheet's gone like greased paper; you can read the back through it.' A killed on 'The rubber in it has oxidised - that's the brown', with the plasticiser assigned a different fate, 'has soaked into the paper'. B inverted on 'She warms a mend from last year, and the film lifts and brings most of the glue with it. On a mend as old as this one, heat does nothing. The glue has gone hard, she says, so only a solvent will move it.' D killed on 'The brown that's in the fibres I can lighten. I don't promise to take it out.' Interleave check: the narration beat 'She turns the certificate to the light.' now sits between the two halves of the quoted speech in paragraph 2, but it falls before the carrying clause and does not separate it from its subject; the key remains fully answerable from the paragraph as printed.

Carrying arithmetic, all of it on the page: 'Torget rymmer femtioåtta stånd', 'Alla som vill ha plats måste söka varje år', 'Fyra platser blev lediga inför förra höstens marknad', 'Sjuttiofyra sökte plats till den marknaden, och alla femtioåtta stånd var upptagna när den öppnade'. Route one: 74 applicants minus 58 filled stalls = 16 unplaced. Route two: 58 minus the 4 vacancies = 54 incumbents renewing, so 74 minus 54 = 20 new applicants competing for 4 places = 16 unplaced. Both routes give 16, and the reference class is unambiguous precisely because 'Alla som vill ha plats måste söka varje år' puts the incumbents inside the 74 rather than beside it. A killed on 'den som stod på torget året innan får stå där igen' - incumbency, not lot. B killed on 'står i Gottfrid Runessons namn och har gjort det längre än platskartan går tillbaka'. C inverted by that same incumbency clause.

Carrying span: the coda 'Flytta hela marknaden, båda dagarna, från och med nästa höst', with the tolerance half supplied by 'De första åren blir sämre. Ingen som räknar kommer fram till något annat, och jag skriver inte under på att det ordnar sig av sig självt.' B killed on 'båda dagarna' in that same coda. C killed on 'Jag var en av de tolv och har alltså inte torghandlarna bakom mig' - she concedes the majority's reasons hold but does not adopt their conclusion. D killed on 'Ett provår vill jag ändå inte ha.'

Carrying span: 'Vem som fick komma in avgjordes inte av hur nära man stod varandra, utan av vad besöket gällde. Prästen släpptes in, och distriktssköterskan, och karlen som skulle värdera skogen. De kom i ärenden som rörde hushållet.' B killed on 'Den som stod hushållet närmast kom sällan längre än till köksbordet' and 'Grannar och släkt satt i köket, oavsett hur långt de hade rest'. C killed on 'Sköterskan var oanmäld varannan gång och visades in ändå.' D killed on the same opening clause, which names errand and expressly denies closeness as the criterion; the esteem reading also has to survive 'Lars Uddén i huset intill blev stående i farstun med mössan i handen', and does not.

Carrying span: 'Sen bar far ut den i köket, för där gick spisen ändå', with 'Dörren till finrummet gick igen som förut' confirming that the watching left the room with the apparatus. A killed on 'Hemma hos oss stod farfars kista i finrummet flera år efter att vår apparat hade burits ut' - the room was still used afterwards. B killed on 'Samma soffgrupp står kvar hos honom.' D killed on 'Hos Hilding Wibbelund stod den i tre vintrar innan huset fick element'.

Worked backwards. A would need the book to open in 1931 and the weir to have been built for the mill; the text supplies neither - 'Since the pass opened in 2011 the trap has been emptied most mornings of the run, the counts written into a hardbacked book', and only 'The weir held water for a mill that stopped in 1931'. C would need a sentence recording a misidentification; the only sentence about the early springs is 'The first nine springs are in one hand, the rest in three others', which is about hands. D would need three hands on the first nine springs; that same sentence gives one. B needs only a netting haul exceeding the trap's dace total, and gets it exactly: 'four hundred-odd of them, more than the trap has held in fifteen years' against '31 dace'.

Worked backwards. A would need the two temperature groups to come out at similar rates; 7 of 11 warm against 5 of 28 cold refuses it. B would need the pools described as restful; 'The pools do not help... there is no quiet corner in them' says the opposite in as many words. C would need size named as the obstacle and build ruled out; the text does the reverse, offering 'deep through the body and carries a dorsal fin like a sail'. D needs only entrants exceeding exits by a majority: 39 in, 'Twelve came out at the top'.

Worked backwards. B would need the fall to be beyond a dace; the text pre-empts this with 'the fall from one pool to the next about 270 millimetres' and 'thinks strength has little to do with it'. C would need a run date and an opening date to collide; neither exists. D would need a refusal to enter singly; 'Nine went in. Five came out at the top' shows individual entry happening. A needs two things and gets both: the wrong-bank arrival, 'they don't come up that side of the river', and the attraction flow dying out, 'Four metres out from the mouth there is nothing of that quarter left to follow.'

Worked backwards, which is where this one is decided. A would need the text to leave force as the operative difference between the two orifices; instead it deliberately equalises the hydraulics with 'came through the same water clear', so force is the one explanation the sentence forecloses. B would need a stated hydraulic purpose; the stated purpose is 'so a fish could go through a wall instead of over it'. D would need all nine walls opened and both openings passable; 'two of the nine cross-walls were cut' and 'it is still packed' deny both. C needs only that position be the sole surviving difference, and 'The other, three walls further up' is the only term the sentence varies.

Worked backwards. A would need the reach above the weir to be a subject; it never appears. B would need the counts to function as support for a thesis; 'What has taken fifteen years to become interesting is what it works for' makes them the object of the enquiry instead, and 'Nobody says the pass does not work' concedes the throughput point rather than arguing it. C would need remediation to be the through-line; only the 2023 orifices and one sentence about a second mouth are on offer. D needs one easy species, two hard ones, and two different causes - trout going up 'without appearing to try', dace who 'don't find it', grayling whose obstacle is that 'Whatever stops them is inside' - and the passage is built on exactly that three-part frame.

Worked backwards. A would need the brown attributed to plasticiser; the text attributes it to rubber, 'The rubber in it has oxidised - that's the brown', and sends the plasticiser elsewhere. B would need heat for hard glue and solvent for soft; the demonstration runs the other way, heat lifting last year's mend and doing 'nothing' on this one, with 'only a solvent will move it' reserved for the hardened glue. D would need the solvent to clear the fibre stain; 'I don't promise to take it out' refuses that. C needs only a stated translucency where glue penetrated, and 'the sheet's gone like greased paper; you can read the back through it' supplies it verbatim. Interleave confirmed: with the narration beat inserted mid-paragraph, the carrying clause still sits inside Fenniscarth's own continuous quotation and is reachable without the surrounding paragraphs.

Worked backwards from what each option demands of the arithmetic. A demands a lottery clause; the text gives a renewal clause, 'den som stod på torget året innan får stå där igen'. B demands a turnover record for plats 1; the text gives permanence 'längre än platskartan går tillbaka'. C demands new applicants outranking old; the renewal clause forbids it. D demands that applicants minus places equal 16. Checked explicitly: capacity 58, vacancies 4, applicants 74, all 58 stalls filled at opening. Subtracting placements from applicants gives 74 - 58 = 16; subtracting renewing incumbents first gives 74 - 54 = 20 new applicants for 4 vacancies, again 16 turned away. The two derivations agree, and the reference class cannot slide, because 'Alla som vill ha plats måste söka varje år' forces the 74 to be the whole pool rather than the new-applicant subset - the only reading that would give a different figure.

Worked backwards. B demands a one-day proposal; the coda says 'båda dagarna'. C demands agreement with the 39; the writer says 'Jag var en av de tolv' while granting that their reasons hold, which is concession, not conversion. D demands a trial year; 'Ett provar vill jag anda inte ha' refuses it by name, with the reason given after it. A demands a move plus an acceptance of the lean years, and both are on the page: 'Flytta hela marknaden, båda dagarna, från och med nästa höst' and 'De första åren blir sämre. Ingen som räknar kommer fram till något annat.'

Worked backwards. B demands intimacy as the criterion; the text denies it twice, in 'avgjordes inte av hur nära man stod varandra' and in 'Den som stod hushållet närmast kom sällan längre än till köksbordet'. C demands notice in advance; 'Skoterskan var oanmald varannan gang och visades in anda' denies it. D demands rank or esteem; the household's nearest neighbour 'blev stående i farstun', while the forest valuer was admitted, so esteem does not track admission. A demands only that the errand decide, and the paragraph opens by saying exactly that and then lists three errand-bearing callers.

Worked backwards. A demands the room be untouched after the set left; 'Hemma hos oss stod farfars kista i finrummet flera år efter att vår apparat hade burits ut' refutes it. B demands furniture replacement; 'Samma soffgrupp star kvar hos honom' refutes it. D demands over ten years in the room; 'i tre vintrar innan huset fick element' caps it well below. C demands that the set end in the kitchen and the evenings follow it, and both halves are given: 'Sen bar far ut den i köket, för där gick spisen ändå', preceded by the watching itself, 'Man frös och man såg på'.
